git cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is already excluded, even with an explicit negation pattern for that exact file. Verified against real `git check-ignore` (git says IGNORED). The TS `ignore` package implements this rule correctly. The Go `github.com/sabhiram/go-gitignore` engine does NOT: it evaluates each pattern line as an independent regex against the full path with no hierarchical/ancestor-exclusion tracking, so the file-specific negation wrongly wins. See local_repo_explorer-wkxb for the discovery.

knownDivergence.reason: go-gitignore has no concept of an already-excluded ancestor directory blocking a per-file negation; it matches each line independently against the full path.

description: a pattern containing a '/' anywhere but at the very end is implicitly anchored to the directory the .gitignore lives in, even without a leading '/' (git docs: a separator at the beginning or middle anchors the pattern). Verified against real `git check-ignore`: src/foo matches at the root but NOT at nested/src/foo. The TS `ignore` package implements this correctly. The Go `github.com/sabhiram/go-gitignore` engine does NOT: getPatternFromLine always prepends an unanchored '^(|.*/)' prefix unless the pattern has an EXPLICIT leading '/', so an internal-slash-only pattern wrongly matches at any depth. See local_repo_explorer-wkxb for the discovery.

knownDivergence.reason: go-gitignore does not implicitly anchor a pattern that contains a non-trailing '/' without an explicit leading '/'; it always allows arbitrary leading path segments unless the pattern starts with '/'.
